Dumb negroes say it never happened and ask where the ships are: cargo ships carried spices and corn before us, carried us as cargo, and after slavery carried cargo again. Why get rid of them?

Then came the dancing of the slaves: the crew played the bagpipe or forced our ancestors to beat out a rhythm while they jumped about, ankles rubbed raw by the leg irons, to keep the human cargo in salable condition. That is Psalms 137:3: those who carried us away captive required of us mirth. At night the cries rose; an enslaved woman explained the howling came from having dreamt they were in their own country and waking in the hold of a slave ship. A strange land indeed.

Millions were carried from Africa to the West Indies, North and South America and Europe, from Luanda, from the Congo, from Loango, where the old maps mark the Jews; the buyers and sellers both knew they were selling outsiders, not the same people. Deuteronomy 28:68 and Psalms 137:3 were fulfilled on those ships.
